newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine ethics bill seen as threat to media.
newsitem.headline: Argentine ethics bill seen as threat to media.

text.p: Argentine opposition politicians on Tuesday criticised measures in a bill that could allow journalists to be imprisoned for two years for publishing public officials' sworn declarations of assets.

The measures are included in a bill on public ethics proposed by a congressional constitutional committee that is due to be debated on Wednesday in the Chamber of Deputies, which is controlled by the governing Peronist Party.
The bill would impose penalties of one month to two years in prison for reporters found guilty of maliciously revealing officials' assets.

"The bill would require (reporters) to reveal information only in the public interest," Radical Party Congressman Jose Dumon told Reuters. "The activity of the press is in the public interest, so it should be able to reveal what it likes."
Dumon said that while he opposed the measures to clamp down on reporting assets, he supported the rest of the bill.
Congressman Raul Zaffaroni of the centre-left Frepaso alliance condemned the measures as "dangerous for the press and for everybody."
But Peronist Congressman Carlos Soria defended the bill, which he said would protect officials from "fraudsters and kidnappers."
Irritated by often critical media coverage, Interior Minister Carlos Corach several months ago proposed the creation of a journalist ethics commission.
The Peronist government has been embarassed several times in recent years by corruption scandals involving senior public officials.
